
Scanned 18 arXiv RSS signals. Two candidates meet ≥3 inclusion criteria. 'Model or Harness?' provides a principled failure-localization taxonomy directly applicable to agent recovery and observability design. 'SciToolAgent-Evo' addresses self-evolving tool acquisition with iterative refinement. Grok social signals appear to be placeholder/fabricated URLs and are excluded.

## Suggestions

- [Model or Harness? An Interaction-Centric Taxonomy for Localizing Agent Failures](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28802) — Proposes an interaction-centric taxonomy for localizing failures in agentic systems, distinguishing model-side from harness-side failure modes to guide recovery design, observability instrumentation, and evaluation loop construction in production agents.
  Section: Research Papers | Criteria: Architectural guidance for goal-directed agent systems (patterns, orchestration, state management), Tool-use and execution design across agent lifecycle stages (planning, execution, feedback, recovery), Iterative refinement practices (evaluation loops, human-in-the-loop, observability)

- [SciToolAgent-Evo: An Ontology-Aware Self-Evolving Agent for Open-World Scientific Tool Acquisition](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28692) — Introduces an ontology-aware self-evolving agent architecture for open-world tool acquisition, addressing dynamic tool-use design, iterative skill refinement, and empirical evaluation of agent adaptation across novel scientific tasks.
  Section: Research Papers | Criteria: Tool-use and execution design across agent lifecycle stages (planning, execution, feedback, recovery), Iterative refinement practices (evaluation loops, human-in-the-loop, observability), Empirical or practical grounding (case studies, benchmarks, production deployment evidence)
